title: Use Case Diagrams
description: Practice quiz on use case diagrams: actors, generalization, <<include>>, and <<extend>>.

questions.question: Actors in a use case diagram ...

options.text: ... can be linked to abstract and non-abstract use cases via associations.
... represent roles of the users of the described system.
... can be linked to each other by inheritance.
... interact with the system in the form of <<include>>-relationships.

questions.question: Which of the following statements are true if use case A is a generalization of use case B?

options.text: B inherits the behavior of A and can override and expand it.
B inherits all relationships from A.
A inherits all relationships from B.

questions.question: The following Use Case Diagram was modeled strictly according to UML2 standard. Which of the following statements are true?

options.text: F cannot be executed without E also being executed.
The behavior of H can be integrated into the behavior of B but does not have to.
Y inherits the behavior of X which Y can either extend or overwrite.
B is also referred to as the included use case.

questions.question: The following Use Case Diagram was modeled strictly according to UML2 standard. Which of the following statements are true?

options.text: Actor A can execute U without any other actors.
X can act as the base use case for Z.
V inherits all associations from U and therefore also inherits all associations from A.

questions.question: How do you model the following situation with a UML2 use case diagram: For an exam, a student and a teacher need to be present. If it is an oral exam, a professor has to act as second examiner.
How do you model the following situation with a UML2 use case diagram: A person goes for lunch. In the course of that it might be necessary that the person withdraws cash from an ATM.
